title: Fill in the Blanks
intro: Fill-in-the-blank questions test either vocabulary (which word fits the meaning) or grammar (which form fits the structure). The method is the same: read the whole sentence for context, decide what the blank needs (a noun? a positive word? a preposition?), then test each option in place. For double blanks, the correct option must make both blanks work.

items.name: Read for context
items.formula: tone and meaning narrow the choice

items.name: Test in place
items.formula: substitute each option and read aloud mentally

items.name: Double blanks
items.formula: BOTH blanks must fit — eliminate on either

topics.name: Vocabulary Blanks
topics.details: Here the blank needs the word that best fits the meaning and tone. Read for positive/negative signals and for collocations (words that naturally go together).

solved.problem: The drought caused a severe ___ of water. (shortage/excess)
She is very ___ and helps everyone. (selfish/generous)
We faced ___ rain during the trip. (heavy/strong)

unsolved.problem: He made a ___ decision after thinking. (wise/foolish)
The teacher ___ the students for cheating. (praised/scolded)
She has a ___ memory and forgets nothing. (sharp/weak)

topics.name: Grammar Blanks
topics.details: Here the blank needs the correct grammatical form — the right tense, agreement, or connector. Use the sentence's time markers and subject to decide.

solved.problem: By the time we reached, the train ___ left. (has/had)
solved.solution: had (past perfect for the earlier past action).

solved.problem: He works hard ___ he may pass. (so that/because)
If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel. (rains/rained)

unsolved.problem: I will call you when I ___ home. (reach/will reach)
He ___ here for five years. (lives/has lived)

topics.name: Prepositions & Articles
topics.details: Many blanks are a single preposition or article. Use fixed combinations and the prepositions of time/place: 'at' a point, 'on' a day/date, 'in' a month/year/place.

topics.name: Double Blanks
topics.details: Double-blank questions give two gaps and four option-pairs. The correct pair must fit BOTH blanks — if either word fails, eliminate the whole pair.

solved.problem: He was ___ tired ___ he slept early. (so/that)
solved.solution: "so … that" (so tired that he slept early).

solved.problem: ___ he is poor, ___ he is honest. (Though/yet)

unsolved.problem: It is ___ hot ___ we cannot play. (so/that)
She is ___ a singer ___ a dancer. (not only/but also)

shortcuts: Read the whole sentence for context before looking at options.
Decide what the blank needs (part of speech, positive/negative, tense).
Use collocations (heavy rain, strong coffee) and fixed prepositions.
Double blanks: the pair must fit BOTH gaps — eliminate on either.
Test each option in place and read it mentally.
mistakes: Choosing a word of the right meaning but wrong collocation.
Ignoring time markers when a grammar form is needed.
Accepting a double-blank pair where only one word fits.
a/an by spelling instead of sound.
pyq: SSC fill-in-the-blank items split between vocabulary fit and grammar form, with a few preposition/article gaps. Context-first reading plus the "both blanks" rule for doubles handles them efficiently.

flashcards.q: "By the time he came, it ___ ended." (had/has)

flashcards.a: Both gaps must fit, or eliminate

summary: Fill-in-the-blanks is context-driven choice: read the sentence, decide what the gap needs (meaning, form or preposition), and test each option in place. Use collocations and fixed prepositions, mind time markers for grammar gaps, and for double blanks accept only the pair that fits both.
